fields.question: Does changing the active observation change the objective?
fields.answer: No. The anchor remains the acceptance objective; the active view exposes diagnostic groups, tiers or related tasks to guide the next training increment.
fields.example: Teaching example: add an eight-needle diagnostic to long-document QA without replacing the original evaluation with easier questions.

fields.question: Why reset marginal-return history after changing observations?
fields.answer: Scores under different observations are not comparable. Subtracting an old easier-task score from a harder-task score confuses measurement change with model regression.
fields.example: Teaching example: moving from an80-point old view to a40-point new view is not a measured40-point training loss; start within-phase comparisons again.

fields.question: Do AdaObs and Harness² evolve the same layer?
fields.answer: No. Harness² edits execution around a fixed model. AdaObs keeps the anchor fixed, changes how training gaps are observed and retrains models in the full study. Neither local diagnostic demonstrates capability gains.
fields.example: Teaching example: grouping failures by context length changes observation; adding a tool retry rule changes the harness.

fields.question: Does one failed L1 diagnostic rule out L1 entirely?
fields.answer: No. Negative memory records a concrete refinement for a current gap. Other feasible L1 options remain eligible; escalation follows only when no L1 option remains.
fields.example: Teaching example: uninformative format groups do not invalidate length groups, and a failure for one gap should not blacklist another gap.

fields.question: Does halving records necessarily halve context tokens?
fields.answer: No. A merged record can be longer. RecordFolder reduces retrieval units; ContextFolder separately compresses each group's text.
fields.example: Teaching example: merging two20-token records into one40-token record halves count but saves no text tokens.

fields.question: Why should an entity in every record add no affinity?
fields.answer: Its IDF log(N/df) is zero when df=N because it does not distinguish events. With no shared entity mass,alpha is zero and affinity returns to cosine.
fields.example: Teaching example: the word user in every record should not link all experiences; a rare project name may identify related ones.

fields.question: Can MemFolder's temporal chains replace MemForest's event trees?
fields.answer: No. MemFolder permits at most one incoming/outgoing edge and reassigns anchor-free chains together. MemForest preserves event-tree hierarchy and retrieves through anchor neighborhoods.
fields.example: Teaching example: a parent event with two child events fits a tree but not a nonbranching matched chain.

fields.question: Why not greedily take the largest link gain?
fields.answer: A local maximum can consume another predecessor's only useful successor. Maximum total gain must respect incoming/outgoing constraints; the local code uses actual Hungarian matching.
fields.example: Teaching example: gains0→2=.9,0→3=.8,1→2=.8 give greedy.9 versus a globally compatible total1.6.

fields.question: Is a faithful memory necessarily useful for future questions?
fields.answer: No. It may omit a key fact or remain undiscoverable in a large store. FIRM separately scores faithfulness,informativeness and retrievability and multiplies them.
fields.example: Teaching example: I entered the room can be faithful while omitting where the keys were placed.

fields.question: Why not use within-candidate variance?
fields.answer: Informativeness and retrievability are constant within a candidate,so their signal lies between candidates. Eq.11 retains it by measuring deviations around the shared group mean before macro averaging.
fields.example: Teaching example: all-one and all-zero candidates each have zero internal variance,but the correct group variance is.25.

fields.question: Do MemOpt and MemFolder optimize the same object?
fields.answer: No. MemOpt decomposes training rewards to improve writer outputs;MemFolder organizes and compresses existing records. Fewer retrieval units do not prove greater faithfulness or fact retention.
fields.example: Teaching example: grouping two records changes structure;lowering credit for a hallucinated token optimizes the writer.

fields.question: May search rank all memories before filtering scope and time?
fields.answer: No. Future or out-of-scope high scores can displace eligible results. Filter end<=query_time and explicit subject/interval first,then rank. This local isolation interface is not identity authentication.
fields.example: Teaching example: with tomorrow scoring1 and yesterday.8,ranking top1 before filtering wrongly returns nothing rather than yesterday.
